_comment: The nav tree for the FoodBridge mock platform.
Each leaf points at a module mockup published by its own team on GitHub Pages.
Nothing here is copied — the platform iframes the live URL, so when a team pushes,
this reflects it on the next load.
clipLeft / clipTop: every module renders its OWN copy of the QA sidebar and header.
The platform owns the sidebar, so each module's sidebar is clipped away by offsetting
its iframe left by clipLeft px inside an overflow-hidden wrapper. clipTop is 0
everywhere on purpose: the module's own header is kept and serves as the app header,
because clipping vertically would push any sticky toolbar out of view.
Every value here was MEASURED in a browser, one destination at a time — see
tools/measuring-clip-offsets.md. Do not infer one from a sibling: four widths are
in use (0, 212, 250, 256), and two screens in the same repo can differ.
fullBleed (optional): a module that is its OWN experience, not an admin sub-
screen — e.g. the customer storefront. When it is active the platform hides
its sidebar (and mobile bar) so the module fills the whole window; clipLeft is
ignored. Use browser back to return to the admin.
deviceFrame (optional): the module is a PHONE app, not a desktop screen.
At lg and above the platform draws its iframe as a phone — 400x860, bezel,
radius 46 — centred on its own canvas, and keeps the sidebar even when the
module is fullBleed. Below lg it changes nothing. Framing the IFRAME means
everything inside, sheets and toasts included, is contained by construction.
urlMobile (optional): a phone-specific screen. The platform loads it instead
of url below 768px, and swaps live when the viewport crosses that width.
mHeaderH (optional, default 56): the height in px of the module's OWN header
on mobile. Below lg the platform draws a single 56px QA-store header that
overlays the module's; this value aligns them (0 = module has no header, so
content is pushed down; 67 = taller header, pulled up and fully covered).
Measured per module in a browser at ~390px.
clipLeftMobile (optional, default 0): horizontal clip to keep on mobile. 0 for
modules that collapse their sidebar into a hamburger; = clipLeft for the few
non-responsive modules that still render a fixed sidebar at phone width.
standalone: destinations that are routable by URL (#/<id>) but NOT shown in
the sidebar. The storefront lives here: it is reached by scanning the Store
QR code (storeQr.targetRoute), not from the admin nav.

storeQr.label: Store QR Code
storeQr.subtitle: Share with customers to let them join your store

nav._why: One home for the owner's two views (21 Sep 2026, product owner): the Control Tower -- what needs you -- and Reports, the dashboard renamed. Their old addresses #/control-tower and #/dashboard still resolve (platform.js aliases).
nav.name: Overview

submenus._why: In the sidebar since 21 Sep 2026; rebuilt 22 Sep 2026 on the five levers (context/control-tower/CONTROL_TOWER_LEVERS.md). Framed like every nav destination -- the shell draws the sidebar and, on a phone, the 56px header; the page draws its lever tabs and the platform footer Tower · Create · EXIT DEMO in place of the shell's EXIT DEMO bar.
submenus.name: Control Tower

nav._why: One item, not a group of one and a half: the submenu held the same name as its parent plus Order Drafts, which is a destination onboarding hands off to rather than a place anyone browses to. Order Drafts is standalone now — addressable at #/order-drafts, absent from the sidebar.
nav.name: Sales Orders

submenus._why: deviceFrame: the route rep's field app, drawn inside a phone on desktop the way Stock Audit frames itself, with the sidebar kept. fullBleed still governs mobile, where it has the screen to itself.
submenus.name: Delivery Management
submenus._whyOwnExitBar: Its own tab bar -- Home, Routes, Follow-up, Reports, EXIT DEMO -- is the footer; EXIT DEMO in it opens the shared exit sheet (delivery-core.js). The shell's bar was drawn over it on a phone (21 Sep 2026, product owner: bring the route delivery footer back).

standalone._whyNoExitBar: Setting a business up is not a demo to be rated half way through. The flow carries its own ways out — its Back, and "Have a look around first" on the first screen — and the bar returns as soon as the flow hands off.
standalone.name: New user onboarding

standalone._why: Out of the sidebar on 18 September 2026, product owner's call. The screen and its module folder are untouched and it stays routable at #/inventory-intelligence, so putting it back in the Inventory group is a two-line change.
standalone.name: Inventory Intelligence

standalone._why: Where "show me around" lands. Before it existed, declining setup opened the import flow — the very question the user had just declined.
standalone.name: Explore

standalone._why: The destination onboarding hands prepared drafts to. Same module as onboarding under ?view=drafts, so it reads the record the flow wrote rather than a second copy of it. Reachable at #/order-drafts; not a sidebar item, because nobody browses to it — the flow sends you.
standalone.name: Order Drafts

hidden.name: Production Settlement
hidden.why: A mockup exists (production-settlement/screens/settlement/index.html) but the QA sidebar has no such item, so it is not in the nav.

hidden.name: Store QR Code
hidden.why: Present: opens a QR that deep-links to the 'retails-overview' standalone storefront.

personas.name: Manufacturer
personas.blurb: Makes and sells — the whole platform

_landing: v5 tests the first session after signing up, so a bare /v5/ opens onboarding rather than the dashboard. Onboarding stays standalone: claiming the landing does not put it in the sidebar.
_frozen: Version 3 — a frozen, self-contained snapshot. Every destination below is a local copy under modules/, not a live GitHub Pages URL, so this folder renders the same whatever the module teams push next. See VERSION.md.
